name: Stausee Zillergründl
kurzbeschreibung: The Zillergründl reservoir is picturesquely nestled in the valley and a popular destination for hiking and enjoying the mountain scenery.
preis: Kostenlos (Mautstraße Zillergrund ca. 12–15 € pro PKW; Linienbus Bärenbad–Staumauer ca. 4 €)
beschreibung:
Overview

Lake Stausee Zillergründl rests as a breathtaking, emerald-to-turquoise alpine reservoir at an altitude of 1,850 meters in the upper Zillertal near the Italian frontier. Impounded in the wild, pristine high valley of Zillergrund, this colossal storage basin holds nearly 90 million cubic meters of glacial meltwater for alpine hydroelectric generation. The architectural centerpiece is the monumental Zillergründl Dam: standing 186 meters high with a crest length of 502 meters, this double-curvature concrete arch dam ranks as the second-tallest dam in Austria and among the grandest engineering achievements in Europe. Guarded by the glaciated 3,000-meter peaks of the Reichenspitz group, the valley captivates both casual walkers and mountaineers. At the secluded head of the lake lies the Hohenaualm chalet—affectionately dubbed "Little Tibet" due to its fluttering prayer flags, stone cairns, and meditative serenity.

Route & Requirements

The reservoir offers splendid, gentle terrain for day hikers, families, and e-bikers. The premier outing is the lakeside walk to "Little Tibet": departing the dam crest, walkers first traverse a 500-meter illuminated rock tunnel before following a wide, virtually level gravel lane along the southern shore to the Hohenaualm (1,863 m; walking time approx. 1 hour, 4 km each way, easy grade T1, stroller friendly). For seasoned alpine trekkers, Zillergründl serves as the gateway to the high-alpine Plauener Hütte (2,363 m; 2 to 2.5 hours climb, 520 vertical meters, moderate grade T2). Sturdy walking shoes and windproof jackets are recommended, as the tunnel and dam wall catch brisk alpine breezes. Leashed dogs are welcome along lakeside paths.

Visit & Arrival

Public transit arrives via ÖBB trains or the historic Zillertalbahn to Mayrhofen terminal. From Mayrhofen, regional bus line 4100 operates frequently from early June through mid-October, traveling through the dramatic Zillergrund gorge directly up to the dam crest. Drivers branch into the Zillergrund at Mayrhofen, following an 18-kilometer scenic toll road to the large parking area at Gasthof Bärenbad (1,450 m). Because the final access tunnel is closed to private vehicles, visitors complete the final 4 kilometers via shuttle bus, bicycle, or on foot.

Tips

Stop at the Hohenaualm ("Little Tibet") for homemade Tyrolean gray cheese (Graukäse), fresh buttermilk, and smoked bacon platters on the timber deck beneath colorful Tibetan prayer flags. Renting an e-mountain bike in Mayrhofen allows you to ride the entire scenic gorge and lakeside path smoothly.
saison: Juni bis Oktober (während der Wintermonate gesperrt)
